messages:
maya: quick idea — spike to evaluate using OPA for resolving auth claims (org/project/sa) at the edge, and emitting a compact decision telemetry tag for routing/quotas. want feedback before i start prototyping.
raf: +1 for a single policy plane. curious about perf — OPA eval per-request? cacheable? :thinking_face: 
lucas: we already have a claim-mapper service that does lookup + enrich. switching to OPA means we either move data into OPA (bad) or call OPA as a decision service (ok).
tara: perf note: any extra RPC on hot path adds p50. can we make OPA part of the local sidecar with a memcached cache for recent principals?
maya: plan is sidecar + in-memory bundle updates using OPA bundles. evaluation stays local. cache key would be <org>:<project>:<sa>:<route>.
simon: what's the advantage vs current claim-mapper? single declarative policy set, easier tests, can express fallback rules (route->model-variant). also aligns with policy-as-code for audits.
raf: telemetry question — we need small decision tags that travel with the request for quota attribution. propose fields: policy_ver, rule_id, decision (allow|deny|fallback). keep tag size < 64 bytes.
maya: exact telemetry format draft: 
```
policy_ver=2026-03-01;rule_id=quota_route_affinity_v2;dec=allow
```
also emit a sampling trace with full decision log to telemetry pipeline (1% default).
sre-oncall: make sure we don't leak internal rule names to customers in logs. full decision logs should be internal-only and redacted for PII.
lucas: rollout? feature-flag gated. step1: sidecar + no-op OPA (mirror decisions to compare). step2: canary region with flagged traffic. step3: flip.
tara: UX: console needs to surface "why traffic used fallback model" to engineers. surface a high-level reason (e.g., "quota-tier-fallback") not raw rule id.
raf: agree. console: expose policy_ver and reason_short. policy internals behind an admin tab.
maya: edge-case: ephemeral SA tokens (ttl < 60s). do not require full bundle update — sidecar should fall back to a tiny local evaluator that only checks token binding.
simon: security check — signing OPA bundles: who signs? ops or keymanager? recommend KMS-signed bundles and verify in sidecar.
maya: yep plan: CI generates bundles, signs via KMS, sidecars verify on fetch.
deploy-bot: deploy queued — spike-opa-sidecar -> staging at 1714010000 by @maya :rocket:
raf: ops/monitoring ask: add a metric policy_eval_ms and policy_eval_cache_hit. for telemetry add rule_hit counts.
sre-oncall: also add a circuit-breaker: if policy eval ms > 10ms for 5m, revert to claim-mapper. avoid hitting SLOs.
tara: i can mock up console screens for the reason_short + policy_ver. will attach designs in #devex.
maya: thanks all — i'll start the spike tomorrow, will post results + perf numbers. cc @raf @lucas for implementation pairing. :thumbsup:
